ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT framework: Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-46-1 and R. 561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). UBO declaration and register: Articles L. 561-46, L. 561-46-1, R. 561-57 and A. 561-2 of the Code monétaire et financier, in conjunction with Articles L. 123-1, R. 123-53 and R. 123-54 of the Code de commerce and Decree No. 2017-1287 of 9 August 2017 (UBO decree), as amended by Decree No. 2020-115. EU sources: Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) and Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AML Package). Public access to the beneficial ownership register is restricted following the CJEU judgments of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20); access remains open to authorities, obliged entities and persons demonstrating legitimate interest. The UBO declaration is filed together with the articles of association through the single business formalities portal and is recorded at the Greffe du tribunal de commerce.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport or national identity card of each beneficial owner, of the legal representative and of the president of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, embassy/consular officer or competent issuing authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague Convention member states (including China as of 7 November 2023, the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom); otherwise Consular Legalization by the Consulate General of France; followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / official company registry extract for any foreign corporate shareholder of the SAS, together with the corporate UBO chain documentation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; officially certified French translation by an approved court-sworn translator (traducteur expert près la cour d'appel)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill, regulated bank statement or registered residential lease) of the UBOs and legal representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, regulated bank or landlord with issuance date within the last three months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of fiscal domicile / tax residence certificate for any foreign shareholder or UBO claiming double tax treaty protection
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax administration of the shareholder's residence state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certified French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of each UBO, legal representative, statutory signatory and expected counterparty against: (i) the consolidated EU financial sanctions list; (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated list; (iii) the French national asset-freezing measures administered by the Direction générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) and associated domestic sanctions databases; (iv) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Blocked Persons List for any USD-denominated Swift wire; and (v) Politically Exposed Person (PEP) and adverse-media datasets. The screening applies a risk-based approach under Article L. 561-4 of the Code monétaire et financier. Any positive hit requires enhanced due diligence, verification of the source of funds, and, where the residual risk cannot be excluded, a Suspicious Transaction Report must be filed with TRACFIN prior to the incorporation filing. All screening results, sources, and timestamps must be archived in the AML compliance file for a minimum of five years from the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Single business formalities portal of the French Government (Guichet unique, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), maintained by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), which administers the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS); public name and register search via data.inpi.fr; historical company extracts via infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (loi Toubon) and Article L. 210-2 of the Code de commerce, the corporate name (dénomination sociale) of a French SAS must be expressed in French or, where a foreign-language element is used, must be accompanied by a French-language rendering in the articles of association. Register filings must be in Latin script, with diacritical marks permitted. Any non-Latin script element must be transliterated into Latin characters for the RNCS, and the French rendering prevails for legal notices and the commercial register. The name must not create a likelihood of confusion with prior company denominations, protected trademarks, or public entity designations.

prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque (requires prior ACPR authorization as it implies a credit institution)
Mutuelle (reserved to registered mutual insurance entities)
Caisse d'Épargne (protected public savings institution denomination)
Chambre de Commerce (reserved to the Chambers of Commerce and Industry)
Croix-Rouge / international organization emblems and names (protected)
Notaire / Avocat / Huissier de justice (regulated liberal professions requiring professional title approval)
État / Ministère / Police / Armée / Préfecture (misleading public-function terms)
France (where the name could mislead as to state sponsorship or as to the national origin of the company; requires additional justification)
stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a common-law style statutory name reservation system; the availability check performed through the Guichet unique and the INPI databases serves as a de facto provisional clearance and the name is fully protected only upon RNCS registration. If the name is refused, the applicant receives a motivated refusal notice. Standard procedure: (i) revise or remove the conflicting token and resubmit the formation application electronically through the same Guichet unique application within 30 days; (ii) in case of collision with a French or European trademark, obtain the trademark owner's written consent or file an opposition before re-filing; (iii) submit a written administrative claim (recours gracieux) to INPI within two months of the refusal; (iv) if the registry persists, apply without court fees to the President of the competent Tribunal de commerce for an order directing registration; and (v) as a final remedy, bring a substantive action before the civil courts to cancel the conflicting earlier right or to compel registration, including the possibility of an interim order (référé). Any final judgment affecting the name is automatically recorded in the RNCS upon production of the judgment to the greffe.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted for a French SAS engaged in ISIC 5911 (commercial 3D animation production, low AML risk). The company must hold a registered office in French territory (Article L. 210-2 of the Code de commerce). A domiciliation contract with a prefecture-approved domiciliation company (Article L. 123-11-2 of the Code de commerce) is lawful provided the provider is approved, hosts no more than 20 companies, and does not operate as a mere letter-box. The registered office must be a physical street address and must appear consistently on invoices, the K-bis extract, contracts, and client-facing materials to preserve commercial substance. A 12-month virtual office contract is typical and is recorded in the RCS.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annualized risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is 2 to 5 percent for a newly formed low-risk SAS without regulated licenses and without public funding. The principal control vectors are unannounced URSSAF verification of employer and business premises (approximately 3 percent of newly registered firms per year), DGFiP tax audits, and TRACFIN AML/CFT checks of domiciliation addresses. Where the company relies exclusively on a virtual office with no production studio or professional premises, the three-year composite risk of a substance inspection rises to approximately 10 to 15 percent, principally to confirm effective management and genuine commercial activity. Maintaining a separate studio lease, documented server infrastructure, and coherent payroll materially reduces this risk.

Publication of the incorporation legal notice in the official legal announcements gazette (annonce légale) of the department of the registered office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory INPI search access fees plus fixed legal review benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-36
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de la Société par Actions Simplifiée
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under Article L. 227-2; capital may be subscribed at 1 Euro
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The first Board of Directors of the Company, a French SAS, resolves as follows: (1) Subscription to the initial share capital of one Euro (1 EUR) represented by one share of nominal value one Euro (1 EUR); (2) Adoption of the registered office at the address specified in the Articles of Association; (3) Appointment of [President Name] as President, [Director Name] as Director, and [Legal Representative Name] as the Company's legal representative; (4) Authorization for the President to execute all acts of incorporation and formalities with the commercial registry. This resolution complies with the provisions of the Code de commerce and is adopted unanimously by the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the INPI website to search for the proposed company name; if available, proceed to reservation; otherwise select an alternative name and repeat the search.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, select a new name and re-submit the availability request

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association including company name, registered office, share capital, directors' details, and purpose; have them reviewed and signed by all shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise documents based on feedback and resubmit for review

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via guichet-entreprises.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed Articles of Association, proof of payment if any, and other required forms through the official online portal; pay the filing fee if applicable; the greffe will process the registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide additional documents or clarifications within the specified timeframe

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Monitor the portal for confirmation; upon approval, receive the SIREN and SIRET numbers; use them to open a corporate bank account and register for VAT.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If delayed, contact the greffe for status update and expedite processing

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Industrie, de la Recherche et de l'Innovation (DRIRE)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating license required for commercial 3D animation services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt due to low environmental impact of digital animation services
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or emissions; comply with general air quality and waste management standards under environmental regulations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural inspections as per local building codes; workplace clearance under Code du travail for occupational health and safety

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the French Ministry for the Economy and Finance; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; business registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must register through Guichet Unique before carrying out taxable supplies in France; the registration grants SIREN/SIRET numbers via INSEE and a French VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) allocated by DGFiP. Non-established taxable persons may also register for VAT through the standard procedure or use the EU OSS/IOSS regimes for distance sales and certain cross-border services; a foreign SAS without a permanent establishment is not subject to French corporate income tax unless it has a fixed base/permanent establishment in France, but it may still be required to register for French VAT if the place of supply is in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available in France. A Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) is mandatorily taxable at corporate income tax (IS) level. Relevant elections/options include: French tax consolidation ('intégration fiscale') for eligible 95%+ groups; French VAT grouping ('assujettis uniques') for financially, organisationally and economically integrated taxable persons; and the parent-subsidiary regime ('régime mère-fille') for qualifying dividend income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No cross-border supplier threshold: a non-established supplier making taxable supplies with a French place of supply must register regardless of turnover, except intra-Community distance sales up to EUR 10,000 may remain taxable in the supplier's EU Member State unless an option is exercised. Domestic 'franchise en base de TVA' relief is available only to French-established small businesses below EUR 85,000 for goods or EUR 37,500 for services; it is not available to foreign entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: French e-invoicing mandate is phased: from 1 September 2026 all established taxable persons must accept structured e-invoices; large and mid-size enterprises issue e-invoices from 1 September 2026 and SMEs/micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027. B2B e-invoices must be routed through Chorus Pro or a registered Dématerialisation Partner Platform (PDP); data are transmitted via REST APIs in the Chorus Pro exchange format. There is no real-time digital stamping; instead the platform performs format validation, extraction, and e-reporting to DGFiP. Accepted formats are Factur-X (ZUGFeRD), UBL and CII complying with EN 16931.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods are zero-rated under Article 262-1 of the French General Tax Code (CGI) only if the exporter establishes through customs declaration and transport documents that the goods physically left the EU within the statutory periods. Commercial 3D animation/VFX services supplied to a non-EU business customer fall outside the scope of French VAT by virtue of the B2B place-of-supply rule, so no French VAT is chargeable; if supplied to a private consumer established outside the EU and effectively used or enjoyed outside the EU, the service may also be outside scope under Article 259 CGI. The supplier must retain credible contractual and technical evidence identifying the foreign customer, IP rights, delivery protocols and payment flows to support non-assessment or zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation / DAU) validated in the DELTA customs system
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing physical export movement
Inward remittance evidence (French law accepts bank transfer/SWIFT confirmation; no notarised Inward Remittance Certificate is required)
Commercial invoice with Incoterms and export/zero-rating references
Packing list and transport contract, where goods are exported
Service agreement, delivery records and IP transfer/licence documentation for 3D animation/VFX services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP regularly scrutinises zero-rated exports and cross-border service non-assessment; missing proof of physical exit or of the foreign customer's business establishment permits reassessment of French VAT at 20%, late-payment interest (0.20% per month under Article 1727 CGI) and penalties from 5% to 40% depending on good faith under Articles 1728-1729 CGI; deliberate concealment or tax-abuse manoeuvres attract up to 80% penalties. Customs fraud (infractions douanières) for false export declarations may additionally trigger criminal fines and imprisonment under the French Customs Code, and export VAT refunds are clawed back with retroactive effect.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full capital account convertibility and current account convertibility as a founding member of the Eurozone and European Union. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted subject to corporate tax filing, withholding tax compliance, and anti-money laundering reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory surrender to the local currency account. French SAS entities must file statistical declarations with customs authorities and record transactions in accounting systems. Foreign currency receipts are converted to euros at prevailing market rates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility of offshore digital EMIs is moderate; French SAS entities may utilize platforms such as Wise B2B, but must establish correspondent banking relationships with French banks and adhere to strict AML/KYC protocols. Direct offshore accounts face regulatory restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors or authorized signatories is generally required for corporate account opening and KYC interviews at French commercial banks. Remote onboarding is limited and typically requires additional documentation and video verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds from high-risk jurisdictions or unexplained cash flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive KYC dossier including beneficial ownership certificates, source of wealth statements, business registration documents, and proof of legitimate commercial activities

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction patterns or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction history, contracts, invoices, and legal opinions confirming compliance with French and international regulations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 messages with purpose codes such as 'CAP' for capital contributions or 'EQTY' for equity investments. Banks require supporting documentation including share subscription agreements, board resolutions, and proof of source of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are cleared using SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) governed by UCP 600. All payments must undergo sanctions screening and comply with French export control regulations.

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Annual Approval of Financial Statements by SAS Shareholders (Décision Collective — Approbation des Comptes Annuels)
stage_5.receiving_authority: Not filed to a regulator; recorded in the SAS Minute Book and prerequisite to the RCS accounts deposit
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year end (court-ordered extension possible if the articles of association so provide or on application to the commercial court)
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual approval decision within 6 months exposes the legal representative to a fine of up to €9,000; the late decision also delays the statutory accounts deposit and may trigger the registry strike-off procedure.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for small businesses (turnover < EUR 10M); Research Tax Credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; tax credit for theatrical productions (for animation films).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (and annexes 2065-A to 2065-SD) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr (mandatory for all companies).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending December 31, deadline is the second business day after May 1st; for other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax (bénéfice net avant impôt)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French-source income only; attach Form 2065-SD for non-resident companies.
Indicate loss if applicable; carryforward rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions and reliefs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty deductions and credits; attach supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development expenses (for CIR claim)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only for French R&D activities; substantiate with technical and accounting records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of tax due, plus 0.5% per month of delay (capped at 10% of tax due); interest at 0.2% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties for failure to file electronically.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (standard rate for non-residents; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥10% for 2 years, or under tax treaties).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, submit Form 5000 (or 5001) to the French tax authority (DGFiP) along with a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. For EU parent-subsidiary directive, provide proof of shareholding and holding period. Relief is applied at source or via refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% (reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if beneficial owner is EU resident and holds ≥25% for 2 years; treaty rates typically 0-10%). Interest: statutory 30% (reduced under treaties, often 0-10%; EU Interest & Royalties Directive applies to interest as well).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (group consolidated turnover or assets) or EUR 50,000,000 (French entity turnover) – whichever is lower; mandatory Local File and Master File.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies economic substance requirements to prevent shell companies. Companies must have real presence (office, employees, management) and perform core income-generating activities in France to benefit from tax treaties and avoid anti-abuse rules (e.g., BEPS Action 6).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false invoicing, or concealment of taxable transactions (e.g., unreported international sales).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalty of 80% of evaded tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they participated in fraudulent acts; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without real economic substance (no employees, no physical office, no actual business activity) while claiming treaty benefits or tax residency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, 40% penalty on unreported income, and potential criminal charges for fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for taxes and penalties if they knowingly used a shell structure; may face criminal prosecution and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures (e.g., customer due diligence, transaction monitoring) or facilitating money laundering through the company's payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 5% of turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned; may be banned from managing companies; civil liability for damages.
